snippet.title: How YouTube Was Created ft. Founder Steve Chen
snippet.description:
This episode takes us back to the earliest days of YouTube, as the founders explain why it was a longshot that succeeded against all odds. When cofounders Steve Chen, Chad Hurley and Jawed Karim left PayPal to start YouTube, it wasn’t even clear that the nascent broadband infrastructure could support playing video in a browser. In a brief period until its acquisition by Google—from its first incarnation as a video dating site to confronting daunting technical and legal challenges—the early story of YouTube is an underdog tale of scrappy upstarts who ended up changing the world. 

Host: Roelof Botha, Sequoia Capital
Featuring: Steve Chen, Jawed Karim, Zahavah Levine, Colin Corbett, Yu Pan

Learn more: https://www.cruciblemoments.com/episodes/youtube

snippet.title: r | p 2006: YouTube: From Concept to Hypergrowth - Jawed Karim
snippet.description:
Less than two years after launch, YouTube has become one the most-visited destinations on the web. With more than 100 million videos served daily, it may be the fastest-growing entertainment website in the history of the World Wide Web. Jawed Karim will explain the thought process and the events that led to the development of YouTube.

Jawed Karim is the co-founder of the popular video sharing website YouTube. Karim attended the University of Illinois from 1997 until 2000, when he joined PayPal to become one of its first developers. He completed his remaining credits at UofI by correspondence and received a B.S. in CS in 2004. In 2005 Karim co-founded YouTube with two friends, co-developing the concept and product, and raising money from Sequoia Capital. He subsequently acted as an advisor to the company and is a graduate student in computer science at Stanford University and an investor in early-stage startups.
Jawed has a long history with ACM and Reflections Projections at UIUC. As a student in 1998, he presented a conference talk, "Practical Graphics Programming," and in 1999, his team placed 2nd in MechMania.
For more information, please visit www.jawed.com.

snippet.title: First Back Flip on Youtube! (House dismount) #2005  #viralvideo
snippet.description:
The first backflip ever uploaded to YouTube.
Yeah… that’s me. User 42 — COBALTGRUV.
Back in 2005, I wasn’t thinking about going viral. I was just sending it off rooftops for the fun of it.
Flip hits at 0:20 if you’re skipping around.
This was the raw start of my COBALTGRUV journey — no safety nets, no sponsors, just a crazy idea, a camera, and a whole lot of heart (and sore legs from all the hard landings). I put a ton of time into filming, editing, and answering comments while juggling a full-time job and everything else life threw at me. All because I loved sharing it with you guys.
After 21 years and over 4 million views, I’ve turned comments to Subscribers & Members only. I’ve matured and sobered up over time, so I’m keeping things a bit more focused these days. The comment section had its wild run — now I’m leaving it open mainly for new subscribers and those old nostalgic memories.
I don’t live there anymore, and I’m not flipping every day like I used to… but the legacy still means something. Over the past 21 years this channel has turned into a mix of old-school flips, truck builds, fishing missions, dogs, and whatever else came along.
A special thanks to my old acquaintance Jawed for giving this flip a push way back when — I hope he’s doing good with whatever he’s into these days. I was genuinely entertained by a lot of the comments over the years, and I really appreciate all the positive feedback from the longtime viewers. It’s been a fun ride.
Big welcome to all my new subscribers too — feel free to drop a comment and say what’s up.
I took a lot of pride in keeping this channel going for two decades. At almost 50, I’m not quitting just yet — I’m shifting my focus to better content and some other projects. I can still land that backflip today, but it feels like the right time to let the younger guys enjoy the spotlight while I wrap this chapter up.
If you want to help me hit that play button milestone after all these years, I’d appreciate you hitting Subscribe. Members get priority replies and early looks. Super Thanks get automatic hearts, comments, and possible pins. Even a small donation or coffee is always appreciated and helps keep things moving.
☕ Buy me a coffee to help keep the content flowing:
https://www.buymeacoffee.com/COBALTGRUV
Stay tough. Keep flipping what life throws at you.
— COBALTGRUV
🤸‍♂️ Thinking of learning a backflip?
Start with strength: squats, planks, push-ups. Stretch your back & hammies. Use a trampoline or foam pit if possible. Jump high, tuck tight, spot the landing. Go slow. Stay safe. Then send it.
